We forget who we really are.

words.gloss: are (кто мы есть = who we are)

lines.trans: We play roles.
The roles of people we don't know.

words.gloss: to us (неизвестных нам = unknown to us)

lines.trans: But the moment of awakening comes.
It tears the endless masks off us.
And lays reality bare.
We weren't ready for it at all.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'illusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в собственных иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often live in our own illusions.

examples.text: Не строй пустых иллюзий, шеф всё равно узнает правду.
examples.trans: Do not build empty illusions, the chef will find out the truth anyway.

meanings.note: From Latin 'momentum' (movement, brief span of time).

examples.trans: At any moment.
One minute, one moment.

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

наступать.gloss: to step on, advance, set in

meanings.en: to step on, put one's foot down
meanings.note: наступать на + acc; ему больно наступать = it hurts him to step

meanings.en: to advance, attack; to arrive/set in (seasons)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to step on, advance, set in', paired with 'наступить'.

examples.trans: But it has become more painful for him to step.

examples.text: Не наступай на ковёр в грязной обуви.
examples.trans: Don't step on the carpet in dirty shoes.

examples.text: Подождите! Но ему наступать стало больнее.
examples.trans: Wait! But it has become more painful for him to step.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'awakening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: But the moment of awakening comes.

examples.text: Но утром неизбежно наступает тяжёлый момент пробуждения.
examples.trans: But in the morning the heavy moment of awakening inevitably comes.

examples.text: Чашка крепкого кофе — лучшее средство для быстрого пробуждения.
examples.trans: A cup of strong coffee is the best remedy for a quick awakening.

meanings.note: Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to exist'.

examples.trans: There exist five stages.
There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I used to come see you often.
He often calls his mum.

examples.text: А меня не помнишь? Я Артурик, я к вам часто приходил.
examples.trans: And don't you remember me? I'm Arturik, I used to come see you often.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
See you tomorrow!
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забыть'.

examples.trans: We're forgetting it!
I always forget my keys.
Go on. We're forgetting!

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'

examples.trans: That's what you said.
That house is old.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Who's there?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'role', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Он сыграл главную роль в спектакле.
examples.trans: He played the lead role in the play.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.
Everyone plays roles.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'известный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('unknown, unfamiliar').

examples.trans: This is unknown, unfamiliar.
A magnificent idea from an unknown person.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tear off, ruin'.

examples.text: Жизнь срывает с нас эти маски.
examples.trans: Life tears these masks off us.

examples.text: Трудная ситуация сразу срывает с людей все притворные маски.
examples.trans: A difficult situation immediately tears all fake masks off people.

examples.text: Мы не имеем права срывать важный вечерний банкет!
examples.trans: We have no right to ruin the important evening banquet!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mask' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: These are foreign masks.

examples.text: Жизнь срывает с нас эти маски.
examples.trans: Life tears these masks off us.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'reality' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Light lays bare the reality.

examples.text: Яркий утренний свет сразу оголяет суровую реальность.
examples.trans: Bright morning light immediately lays bare the harsh reality.

examples.text: Пора наконец вернуться из мечтаний в обычную реальность.
examples.trans: It is time to finally return from daydreams to ordinary reality.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Совсем не.
Совсем не.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.
He's completely alone.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

examples.trans: I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.
Right, I'm ready!

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'конечный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('endless').

examples.trans: They were endless.

examples.text: Эти разговоры на кухне казались бесконечными.
examples.trans: Those conversations in the kitchen seemed endless.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто бесконечный поток гостей.
examples.trans: We have a simply endless stream of guests today.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'bare, expose'.

examples.trans: Light lays bare the reality.

examples.text: Яркий дневной свет сразу оголяет любую пыль в зале.
examples.trans: Bright daylight immediately exposes any dust in the hall.

examples.text: Не стоит так открыто оголять свои слабые места перед конкурентами.
examples.trans: You should not expose your weak spots so openly in front of competitors.
